plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Fields in Provence turn into rolling ribbons of violet at the start of summer. Silvery, fragrant foliage carries slender spikes of tiny blossoms. Bees crowd the rows and the warm air smells sweet and herbal.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, with peak bloom usually in mid-July
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: South Africa's national flower is the largest of all the proteas. Its dinner-plate-sized head is a crown of silky, pointed bracts around a central cluster of true flowers. It opens in the cool, damp southern winter, when most of the world's gardens are in summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, roughly June to October
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa, including Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
plants.funFact: Proteas belong to an ancient plant family that dates back to when the southern continents were joined. The flower head is built to survive fire, and the plant resprouts from a woody base after wildfires.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Huge, goblet-shaped blooms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. Each flower opens in the morning and closes at night, and lasts only about three days. Ponds in summer fill with these blooms.
plants.location: Warm-temperate and subtropical ponds and lakes of Asia, widely grown in water gardens
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves are covered in microscopic bumps that make water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt with it. This 'lotus effect' has inspired self-cleaning paints and fabrics.
